chapter: Los Angeles, Chet Baker and film beginnings
title: Al Cohn's career and Flo
summary: Mandel explains why Al Cohn gave up writing to become a full-time saxophonist after losing sight in one eye, and mentions Flo, Ella Mae Morse's sister.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, he’s one of the few, well I guess Al Cohn didn't play much for years.

He didn't play much for years and he didn't really start playing his best until he became a full-time saxophone player, is when he finally gave up writing, which I really hated to see. I used to beg him to keep writing but he had spent so many years trying to raise a family and writing music he didn’t like and his eye, he only had one eye after 1949 or ‘50 and as a matter- of-fact he was out of the business for a while working for his father, who I think was – Dave Cohn was in the garment business at the time. And when he came with Elliot that was his first foray back into music, he had been out of music for a while, after his eye operation. And so he made it on one eye since then, and he used to do have to shows for Ralph Burns and you know he was just doing a whole lot of music he didn’t like and…

When he finally got free of his marriage and a whole lot of other things and the kids were grown up enough, he decided he wasn't gonna write anymore music and his one eye was just killing him. He became a full-time saxophone player and that’s what he ended up spending his life and when he started doing that and put all his energy in the saxophone, whoo man!
He was always good before that but became more than good after that.
I think it’s one of the small ironies of the jazz business that he ended up marrying George Handy’s ex-wife.
Yeah, Flo, who is also a talented composer.
Very, yeah and you know who’s sister she was?
Ella Mae Morse’s kids sister, yeah. I knew her from the time she was 16 years old, wonderful girl.
Very talented composer and a wonderful singer.
I loved the way she sang. Yeah.
